chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about an epidemic that occurs in a region of Egypt, so a man moves to another region, or it is in a city so he leaves it for another; he said: There is no harm. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) only prohibited that because of a place called Rabee'ah that was opposite the enemy, and the epidemic struck them, so they fled from it. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Fleeing from it is like fleeing from the march (of the enemy army), out of dislike that their positions become empty.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to leave a city during an epidemic according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that fleeing an epidemic is permissible, distinguishing the general prohibition of 'fleeing the plague' from its specific historical context during the Caliphate of Umar, where it was feared soldiers would abandon their defensive posts against the Romans. This hadith underscores the Shia scholarly principle of understanding prophetic traditions within their precise temporal and situational frameworks rather than as absolute, context-independent commands.
